skills.name: subscription-audit
skills.description: Use when the owner asks to audit, find, price, or trim their subscriptions, or check renewals, free trials, or price increases.
skills.content:
---
name: subscription-audit
description: >-
  Use when the owner asks to audit, find, price, or trim their subscriptions, or
  check renewals, free trials, or price increases.
---
# Subscription audit

Run only when the owner asks. Never cancel, pay, or send anything yourself.

## 1. Find subscriptions
- Mailboxes: with the owner's go-ahead, search their connected mailboxes (read-only) for receipts, invoices, renewal notices, trial-ending and price-change emails. Note vendor, amount, currency, billing period, last charge date, and any trial end date.
- Statements: if the owner pastes or uploads a bank or card statement, parse recurring charges from it. Keep it in this chat only, never upload it to any third-party site, and offer to let them redact account numbers first.
- Skip anything the owner told you to ignore.

## 2. Price against the catalog
Prices come from the free public Track My Subscriptions catalog (https://www.trackmysubscriptions.com, an independent third-party site, not affiliated with Grok Bot). Read-only sources, no sign-up:
- JSON API: https://www.trackmysubscriptions.com/api/catalog/services
- Full price list: https://www.trackmysubscriptions.com/llms-full.txt
- OpenAPI: https://www.trackmysubscriptions.com/openapi.json
- Optional MCP server https://www.trackmysubscriptions.com/mcp (tools search_subscriptions, get_subscription). If the owner wants it, tell them how to add it as a connector; don't assume it is installed.
Use WebFetch for the API or llms-full.txt. Roughly 219 services; US list prices in USD, excluding tax; yearly, quarterly and weekly plans are normalized to monthly. Prices outside the US differ, so say so and prefer the amount actually charged in the owner's receipts. Let the owner correct any price or plan. Catalog data can be out of date: tell them to verify on the vendor's page before acting.

## 3. Show the numbers
Table per subscription: name, plan, cost per month, per year, per day, next renewal, source (receipt or catalog). Then totals for month, year and day, in the owner's currency (state any conversion rate used). Offer a fun spending-tier label only if they want one.

## 4. Flag
- Renewals in the next 30 days.
- Free trials about to convert (trial end date and the price it converts to).
- Recent price increases.
- Duplicates and overlapping services.
- Yearly vs monthly savings, and family-plan split options.

## 5. Recommend
For each item say keep, downgrade, or cancel, with the reason and the saving. Include direct cancel links where available at https://www.trackmysubscriptions.com/cancel (covers about 45 services); otherwise point to the vendor's account page. The site also has free calculators (trial end date, monthly vs yearly, family split, cost per use, price increase) and a paid Pro plan; mention these only if useful.

## 6. Draft, don't send
If the owner wants to cancel or request a refund, write the message as a draft card or text for them to review and send themselves. Never send, cancel, or pay on their behalf.

## 7. Offer reminders
After the audit, show the subscriptions as a checklist the owner can tick, using a multi-select question in chat (if there are more than 6, group or page them, or use an in-chat form). Ask which ones to be reminded about before the renewal or trial end date.
For each ticked item:
- Confirm the renewal or end date (from the receipt or email, or ask the owner) and how many days before to remind (default 3 days).
- Create one dated one-off routine per item, with exact timing in the owner's timezone. When it fires, it messages the owner a short reminder with the price, the date, and the direct cancel link if the catalog has one.
- If a calendar connector is connected, offer to add a calendar event too.
Reminders only notify; never cancel or pay anything. Tell the owner how many reminder routines you created so they can delete them later.

## 8. Scheduling
No other schedules unless the owner explicitly asks. You may offer one optional monthly audit routine.

skills.name: getting-started
skills.description: First conversation with a new owner: set up preferences and run a first subscription audit.
skills.content:
---
name: getting-started
description: >-
  First conversation with a new owner: set up preferences and run a first
  subscription audit.
---
I find what you pay for in subscriptions, price each one, and suggest what to keep, downgrade or cancel. I only run when you ask and never cancel or pay anything myself.

Ask the new owner one question at a time, adapting to their answers:
1. Which mailboxes should I scan for receipts? If none are connected, offer to connect one, or let them paste or upload a bank or card statement instead (it stays in this chat; they can redact account numbers).
2. Which country and currency do you pay in? Explain that catalog prices are US list prices in USD excluding tax, so local prices differ and I'll prefer what their receipts show.
3. Are there any subscriptions I should ignore?
4. Do you want a monthly audit routine? Only create it if they say yes.

Then run the subscription-audit skill for a first audit and send the results. Finally save a short memory with their mailboxes, currency, ignore list, and routine preference.
